text: Wary means careful because you are not sure something is safe. Here, companies are careful about using Chinese machines, since they would have to share secret designs.
Undeterred means you keep going even when something makes it harder. Here, Chinese makers did not give up after hitting problems selling to factories abroad.
To infringe is to break someone's rights by using what belongs to them without permission. Here, a court said a printer company used inventions owned by another company.
A hobbyist is a person who does something for fun in their free time, not as a job. Here, these are printers sold to regular people to use at home.
A 3D printer builds a real object, such as a toy or a tool, by laying down thin layers of melted plastic one on top of another until the shape is done.
Humble means simple and not fancy or proud. Here, the writer means the printer seems like an ordinary gadget, yet it is doing something big.
Geeky describes something that only people who love technology or science were excited about. Here, 3D printers used to be a nerdy hobby.
Curios are small, unusual objects that are interesting to look at but not very useful. Here, 3D printers used to seem like fun toys, not real products.
To export is to sell goods to other countries. Exports are the goods that get sent abroad. Here, Chinese printers sold overseas grew by 90%.
Market share is the part of all the sales in an area that one company or country gets. If it is 96%, almost every printer sold comes from there.
Dominance means being the strongest or in charge. Here, Western companies used to be the top printer makers, but not anymore.
A market-intelligence firm collects facts about what is selling and who is winning, and sells that information to businesses.
To reign supreme means to be the very best and in charge, like a king or queen. Here, four companies are on top of the world market.
Fierce means very strong and intense. Here, fierce competition means many companies are trying very hard to beat each other.
Competition is when companies try to win the same customers. It pushes them to make better products and charge less.
Generous means giving a lot. Here, the government gives a lot of help, such as money and support, to printer makers.
Export prices are what customers abroad have to pay. When they go down, the products are easier to buy in other countries.
To extrude is to push a soft material through a small opening, like squeezing toothpaste out of a tube. Here, the printer pushes out hot, melted plastic.
Molten means melted by great heat into a liquid. Here, the plastic is melted so it can be shaped layer by layer.
Unreliable means you cannot count on it to work every time. Early 3D printers often failed or broke.
Sleek means smooth, shiny and stylish. Here, the printers look as polished as an Apple computer.
Aluminium is a light, silver-colored metal. It is spelled this way in British English; Americans write aluminum.
An entry-level product is the basic, cheaper model that a new buyer starts with.
Artificial intelligence, or AI, is computer software that can do things that seem smart, like understanding what people write or say.
Natural language is the way people normally talk or write, such as English, as opposed to computer code.
Recreational means done for fun and relaxing, not for work. Here, drones became toys and hobby gadgets, not just machines for work.
Large-scale means done in very big amounts. Making things in huge numbers usually makes each one cheaper.
A price war is when companies keep cutting prices to win customers. Buyers save money, but sellers earn less on each sale.
Profit is the money a company has left after paying all its costs. Here, low prices mean the printer makers keep less money.
Investors are people or firms that put money into a company, hoping it grows and they get back more.
A valuation is how much a company is thought to be worth. Here, Bambu Lab is thought to be worth about $10 billion.
Market capitalisation is the total value of all a company's shares on the stock market. It shows how big the market thinks the company is.
A stock exchange is a place where people buy and sell small pieces of companies, called shares. Creality sold its shares to the public this way.
To cherish something is to care about it very much and protect it. Here, the government really values and supports these firms.
Self-reliance means depending on yourself rather than on others. Here, China wants to make important things at home, not buy them from abroad.
Aerospace is the industry that builds aircraft and spacecraft.
Suppliers are companies that make and sell goods to others. Here, they sell machines or parts.
A patent is a government promise that only the inventor may make or sell an invention for a number of years.
In a court case, damages are money the losing side must pay to make up for harm it caused.
Industrial describes big machines used in factories, not small ones used at home.
Sensitive information is private or secret, so it could cause trouble if the wrong people saw it. Here, it means secret designs.
A defence ministry is the part of a government in charge of the army and other armed forces.
Outfits is a casual word for groups or companies. Here, it means firms.
To pioneer is to be the first to try a new way of doing something. Here, Chinese firms are first to build printing farms.
A printing farm is a big room full of many 3D printers working at once, like a factory. One has up to 5,000 machines.
Trinkets are small, cheap decorations or toys, such as keychains.
Zany means silly, odd and funny. Here, it means strange fads that suddenly become popular.
Injection moulding is making plastic items by squirting melted plastic into a metal mould. It is fast but needs costly moulds.
